transcript.text: AEG IKB64301FB induction hob keeps beeping and showing Er03 then switches off. Pan of pasta boiled over just before.

The 'Er03' code isn't in my standard database for AEG hobs, but given that a pan boiled over immediately before it happened and the hob is now beeping and switching off, this suggests the overheating protection has been triggered. Induction hobs have cooling fans to keep the electronics safe; if a spill gets underneath or into the vents, it can cause a short or block airflow, leading to an emergency shutdown. Please do these owner-safe checks:
1. Isolate the hob: Turn off the power at the wall switch or consumer unit (fused spur) for at least 30 minutes to let it cool and reset any electronic locks.
2. Check for spillage: Look carefully around the edges of the glass surface. If you see dried food or liquid residue near the vents or underneath the rim, this is likely the cause. Do not use water yet; just note if it looks blocked.
3. Listen to the fan: After restoring power and turning on a zone (even at low heat), listen closely for a whirring sound from the front edge of the hob. If you hear no fan noise at all, the cooling fan may have failed or been damaged by the spill. If there was significant boil-over into the vents, it often needs professional cleaning to remove moisture and debris from inside the unit. If the hob is completely dry and the fan runs normally but the error persists after a full reset, we can look at other causes.

There was starchy water across the touch slider, so I wiped it dry and switched it off at the wall for about 5 minutes. It works again now. I couldn't tell you about the fan noise, I didn't notice either way.

Water near the plug or socket is dangerous. Please don't touch the plug, socket or machine if they or your hands are wet. If you can do it safely, switch off the circuit at the consumer unit (fuse box), keep away from the water, and don't use the machine again until a qualified electrician or appliance engineer has checked it. That is good news. It sounds like the starchy water on the touch slider caused a temporary fault or short that triggered the safety shutdown; wiping it dry and isolating the power allowed the system to reset. Is there anything else I can help you with today?

candidates: Cooling fan failure or blocked ventilation (medium)
Main PCB fault (less likely without other signs) (low)

reading.symptom: keeps beeping and showing Er03 then switches off

plan: Already given by the customer, never ask for it again: make AEG; model IKB64301FB; code ER03.
The fault they reported is: "keeps beeping and showing Er03 then switches off". Keep to it: never describe a symptom, result or state they have not told you.

Stage 1 (broad help): say what could cause this, most likely first, as possibilities rather than certainties, including simple causes (settings, loading, detergent, installation, or normal behaviour) where they fit. Then give the safe checks that best tell those causes apart (most useful and simplest first, usually two to four), each with why it helps and what each result would mean; or, if one question would settle it sooner, ask that. Do not ask for the model number in this reply. Do not tell them to buy, order or replace a part yet.

Explain what the error code means using ERROR CODES. If ERROR CODES does not resolve it, say plainly that you cannot confirm what it means on their model (it may not be an error code at all, for example part of the model name), never guess a meaning, and work from the symptoms.
